purpose: Structured, multimodal content restriction database — extends DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md's existing non-negotiables (no violence, no fear, positive tone) with contextual, per-modality rules the generation pipeline can actually check against, rather than relying on an agent to remember channel policy unaided. No equivalent system existed before this file (confirmed by repository search, 2026-08-05).

restrictions.script_mention: CONTEXT_ONLY — only if a real, cited educational lesson about halal/haram food genuinely requires it (e.g. a topic directly about food rules), never as incidental scene detail
restrictions.visual_depiction: NEVER_GENERATE — no pig characters, no pig toys, no pig imagery anywhere
restrictions.audio_depiction: NEVER_GENERATE — no pig sounds/oinks used as incidental sound design
restrictions.background_element: NEVER_GENERATE — must not appear as incidental background animal/farm-scene decoration
restrictions.promotion_or_normalization: NEVER_GENERATE — no framing that normalizes eating it
allowed_contexts: A cited, evidence-based lesson explicitly about halal/haram dietary rules, age-appropriate, with real Quran citation per verification_pipeline.md
replacement_strategy: Use sheep, goats, cows, chickens, or other common halal farm animals instead of pigs in any farm/animal scene

evidence_references.note: prohibition of swine flesh, one of 4 Quranic references
most comprehensive dietary prohibition list including swine

restrictions.cross_check_note: 4 independent verse references converge across 6+ independently-authored sources (Quranic Arabic Corpus/Leeds University academic resource, and multiple Islamic educational sites) — not a single-source claim.
restrictions.notes: Full Quran verse text for these 4 references has not yet been ingested into quran_verses.json — this restriction record cites the verse reference, not a canonical quotation. Retrieved 2026-08-05.

restrictions.script_mention: ALLOWED — Allah may be referenced by name/attribute in narration, dialogue, dua, exactly as the repository's existing Islamic reference data already does
restrictions.visual_depiction: NEVER_GENERATE — no face, no form, no anthropomorphic representation, no symbolic stand-in presented as 'this is Allah'
restrictions.audio_depiction: NEVER_GENERATE — no voice performance presented as Allah speaking in first person as a character
restrictions.song_lyrics: ALLOWED to reference Allah by name/attribute in lyrics (as existing lyrics_and_song.md outputs already do); NEVER_GENERATE any visual pairing that depicts Allah during the song
allowed_contexts: Verbal/textual reference by name and attribute only — light, nature, or narrative cues implying Allah's presence without figurative representation are acceptable stylistic choices, not a religious requirement themselves
prohibited_contexts: Any scene, thumbnail, or prop implying a literal visual form for Allah
replacement_strategy: Use light, open sky, warmth, or the reactions/words of characters to convey a moment of connection to Allah, never a figure

evidence_references.reference: Quran 4:48 (shirk as the one unforgivable sin, cited context for the idolatry-prevention rationale)
evidence_references.note: general Quranic basis for avoiding anything resembling idol-representation

restrictions.cross_check_note: Near-universal consensus across Sunni Islamic practice; multiple independent sources confirm.
restrictions.notes: This is the least disputed of all depiction rules — essentially unanimous. Kept at NEVER_GENERATE with high confidence.

restrictions.canonical_name: Visual depiction of Prophets (including Prophet Muhammad ﷺ)
restrictions.script_mention: ALLOWED — Prophet stories may be narrated (per existing prophets.json entries: prophet_nuh, prophet_yunus etc.), events described, dialogue only where repository evidence supports it (per DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md's fiction-vs-fact separation)
restrictions.visual_depiction: NEVER_GENERATE — no face, no full-body figurative depiction of any Prophet, in any art style including the channel's own Pixar/Illumination cartoon style
restrictions.audio_depiction: CONTEXT_ONLY — narrator describing events is fine; a voice performance in first person AS the Prophet speaking new invented dialogue is NEVER_GENERATE unless the words are a direct, cited quotation
restrictions.song_lyrics: CONTEXT_ONLY — may reference a Prophet's story/lesson by name and event, never invented first-person Prophet dialogue as lyrics
allowed_contexts: Narrated retelling of Quran-supported events, symbolic/environmental visual storytelling (e.g. the whale, the ark, the setting) instead of a figure
prohibited_contexts: Any character design, thumbnail, or animation showing a Prophet's face or body
replacement_strategy: Show the event's setting, objects, other characters' reactions, symbolic light/silhouette from behind, or narration over an environment shot instead of a figure — this repository's existing prophet_yunus/prophet_nuh entries already avoid this by focusing narration on event and lesson, not physical depiction

evidence_references.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Dress/Clothing (figurative-image hadith)
evidence_references.note: hadith-based prohibition on images of living beings, applied with particular strictness to Prophets — general reference only, exact hadith_id not yet in repository (see notes)

restrictions.cross_check_note: Broad, near-universal Sunni consensus, confirmed across multiple independent academic and educational sources. Sources also note real historical exceptions (Persian/Turkish miniatures, Shia depictions of Ali) and Sunni/Shia variance on companions specifically — this repository's channel policy takes the stricter, more universally-accepted NEVER_GENERATE position for the core Prophet category rather than adjudicating between traditions.
restrictions.notes: The specific underlying hadith text has not been ingested into hadith.json with a real hadith_id yet — this restriction is source_verified at the policy level (multiple independent confirmations that this consensus exists) but the exact hadith citation is a Batch 02 task, tracked in roadmap/planned_features.md. Companions/Ahl al-Bayt depiction is marked REVIEW_REQUIRED separately below rather than assumed identical to the Prophet rule.

restrictions.canonical_name: Companions and other revered historical Islamic figures (depiction)
restrictions.script_mention: ALLOWED per existing companions.json entries (narrated, not depicted)
restrictions.visual_depiction: REVIEW_REQUIRED — sources found during this pass note real Sunni/Shia variance specifically here (Shia tradition permits depicting Ali; Sunni tradition generally extends the Prophet-depiction caution to companions and wives too) — not something this system should resolve on its own
restrictions.song_lyrics: ALLOWED to name/reference by story, not depict
replacement_strategy: Until reviewed: treat the same as restriction_003 (Prophets) as the conservative default — narrate, don't depict
restrictions.cross_check_note: Confirmed real, documented scholarly/sectarian variance exists — this is exactly the kind of disputed-scope item that must not be resolved by this system per its own governing instructions.
restrictions.notes: Defaulting to the conservative treatment (no depiction) as a channel-policy choice while REVIEW_REQUIRED remains the formal status — this is a channel-policy default, not a claim that the stricter position is the only correct one.

restrictions.script_mention: NEVER_GENERATE — reuses DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md's existing non-negotiable, not a new rule
replacement_strategy: Conflicts stay emotional/social per conflict_library.json's existing design — a lost toy, a disagreement, never physical harm
restrictions.cross_check_note: Not an Islamic-evidence question — this is this repository's own existing child-safety/brand policy, already stated in DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md's Story non-negotiables. No new research needed; reused, not duplicated.
restrictions.notes: category correctly marked CHILD_SAFETY, not ISLAMIC_RESTRICTION — this prevents a future agent from mistaking existing brand-safety policy for an Islamic ruling, per section 34-K's explicit instruction.

restrictions.script_mention: NEVER_GENERATE — reuses DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md's existing no-fear non-negotiable
allowed_contexts: Gentle worry/concern per emotion_database.json's existing 'gentle_fear' entry — deliberately capped low-intensity, not the same as frightening content
prohibited_contexts: all beyond the capped gentle_fear entry
replacement_strategy: Use emotion_database.json's existing gentle_fear intensity cap

restrictions.script_mention: NEVER_GENERATE for incidental content; CONTEXT_ONLY for an evidence-cited educational lesson
restrictions.background_element: NEVER_GENERATE — no incidental bottles/glasses in background scenes
replacement_strategy: Juice, water, milk, tea for any beverage scene

evidence_references.note: Direct, primary-verified prohibition — both khamr (intoxicants) and maysir (gambling) named explicitly in the same verse.
evidence_references.arabic_text: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ إِنَّمَا ٱلْخَمْرُ وَٱلْمَيْسِرُ وَٱلْأَنصَابُ وَٱلْأَزْلَٰمُ رِجْسٌ مِّنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ فَٱجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
evidence_references.translation: O you who believe! Intoxicants, gambling, idols, and drawing lots for decisions are all evil of Satan's handiwork. So shun them so you may be successful.
